item.title: Why the ball is in Kim Jong-un’s court on a meeting with Donald Trump
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s absence from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering in Shenzhen could indicate that a meeting with Donald Trump will not take place in the foreseeable future. Analysts said it was a vastly different geopolitical and logistical situation from Trump’s first term, when the two leaders met three times. Sydney Seiler, senior adviser to the Korea chair at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies, said Kim was trying to “lock in” his nuclear weapons...

item.title: Hong Kong police hunt man for alleged theft of HK$1.9 million in cameras and lenses
item.description: Hong Kong police are searching for a man suspected of stealing 61 cameras and 55 lenses worth nearly HK$1.9 million (US$242,300) from a shop in Causeway Bay, the South China Morning Post has learned. A source familiar with the case said on Friday that the store was Fortress, an electronics and home appliance retailer, in Times Square shopping centre. The store’s manager, who reported the case, said the suspect had stolen the items over two months before going incommunicado on November 18,...

item.title: Debate erupts over China university’s US$4.6m smart system tracking ‘head-raising rates’
item.description: An elite university in eastern China has spent more than 30 million yuan (US$4.6 million) installing a smart classroom system to track students’ “head-raising rate” – an indicator intended to reflect their attentiveness during lectures – and link it to their academic scores. Nanjing University, in Jiangsu province, came under fire after some students shared on social media that the smart system would go into operation in the first week of November, Haibao News reported.
